info.title: Astra Astrology API
info.description:
Backend for the **Astra Astrology** platform — astrology, numerology and
astrologer consultations.

* `auth` — registration via email+password (OTP verified) and Google sign-in,
  kept in sync between MongoDB and Firebase Auth
* `health` — liveness and readiness

get.description: The cheapest endpoint to use as a keep-alive target.

schema.title: Response Ping Api V1 Ping Get

get.summary: Check whether an email is free (checks MongoDB and Firebase)

post.summary: Start sign-up — checks both stores, then emails an OTP
Verify the code and create the account in Firebase + MongoDB
Sign in with email and password
Google sign-in — registers on first use, signs in after that
Start a password reset — emails a code to a registered address
Finish a password reset — code plus the new password
Change my password while signed in

AstrologerCreate.title: AstrologerCreate
AstrologerCreate.description:
What an admin fills in to open an astrologer's account.

No password field: one is generated and emailed to the astrologer, because
nobody — not even the admin — should be choosing someone else's password.

initial_password.description: Only filled in when the welcome email could not be sent, so the admin can pass the password on another way.

AstrologerProfile.description: The astrologer's own view, and the admin's.

AstrologerPublic.title: AstrologerPublic
AstrologerPublic.description:
What the website and app may show about an astrologer.

Deliberately narrower than `AstrologerProfile`: no email, phone, bank
details, commission or account status — this is served to anyone.

AstrologerUpdate.title: AstrologerUpdate
AstrologerUpdate.description:
What the astrologer may change about themselves.

Rates, commission and the curation flags are absent on purpose — those are
the platform's to set, not the astrologer's.

ProfileUpdate.title: ProfileUpdate
ProfileUpdate.description:
Partial update. Only the fields present in the body are touched.

`extra="forbid"` is deliberate: `email` is the sign-in identity and is not
editable here, so an attempt to change it fails loudly instead of being
quietly dropped. It also turns a misspelt field name into an error rather
than a silent no-op.
